paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרְב֥וּ יְמֵֽי־דָוִ֖ד לָמ֑וּת וַיְצַ֛ו אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: Now the days of David drew near that he should die; and he charged Shelomoh his son, saying,

notes.official: *wayyiqrəḇû yəmê-ḏāwiḏ lāmûṯ* 'Now the days of David drew near that he should die', the deathbed formula used of Ya'aqov at Gen 47:29. *wayəṣaw* 'and he charged': a testament (cf. Josh 23; Gen 49).

paragraphs.text: אָנֹכִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחָזַקְתָּ֖ וְהָיִ֥יתָֽ לְאִֽישׁ׃

i18n.en: "I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong therefore, and show yourself a man;

notes.official: *ʾānōḵî hōlēḵ bəḏereḵ kol-hāʾāreṣ* 'I am going the way of all the earth', a euphemism for death shared with Josh 23:14. The ASV 'earth' is kept, since 'the way of all the land' would obscure the idiom; the central `eretz` default does not apply. *wəḥāzaqtā wəhāyîṯā ləʾîš* 'Be strong therefore, and show yourself a man'.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֞ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לָלֶ֤כֶת בִּדְרָכָיו֙ לִשְׁמֹ֨ר חֻקֹּתָ֤יו מִצְוֺתָיו֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֣יו וְעֵדְוֺתָ֔יו כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֑ה לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֗יל אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּפְנֶ֖ה שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: and keep the charge of YHWH your Elohim, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, and his ordinances, and his testimonies, according to what is written in the law of Moshe, that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn yourself;

notes.official:
*wəšāmartā ʾeṯ-mišmereṯ YHWH* 'and keep the charge of YHWH': the series charge, statutes, commandments, ordinances, testimonies is a Deuteronomistic expansion of the four-noun formula of Gen 26:5 (central `mishmeret-mitzvot-chuqim-torot-fourfold-covenant`, which cites this verse; ASV order and wording kept).

*bəṯôraṯ mōšeh* 'in the law of Moshe' (ASV 'law'): *tôrâ* means 'instruction, teaching', but in this Deuteronomistic phrase (Josh 8:31; 23:6; 2 Kgs 14:6; 23:25) it names a written law-book, so 'law' is kept. Moshe = Moses: the Kings volumes transliterate names, and the exodus-woh 'Moses' is a single-book exception that is not extended (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *ləmaʿan taśkîl* 'that you may prosper' (or 'act wisely').

paragraphs.text: לְמַעַן֩ יָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַי֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם־יִשְׁמְר֨וּ בָנֶ֜יךָ אֶת־דַּרְכָּ֗ם לָלֶ֤כֶת לְפָנַי֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת בְּכָל־לְבָבָ֖ם וּבְכָל־נַפְשָׁ֑ם לֵאמֹ֕ר לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: that YHWH may establish his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their being, there shall not be cut off from you,' he said, 'a man on the throne of Yisra'el.'

notes.official:
*lāleḵeṯ ləp̄ānay beʾĕmeṯ* 'to walk before me in truth': the covenantal walking formula (central `hithallekh-lefanai-patriarchal-walking-before-elohim-covenantal-formula`, which cites this verse). *bəḵol-ləḇāḇām ûḇəḵol-nap̄šām* 'with all their heart and with all their being' (ASV 'soul'), the Deuteronomic pair of Deut 6:5. *nepeš* here is the whole living self (HALOT; Wolff, *Anthropology of the Old Testament*, 1974), and 'being' renders it without the dualist 'soul' that the corpus avoids (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`; central `nefesh-chayah`); Alter uses 'being' at Deut 6:5.

*lōʾ-yikkārēṯ ləḵā ʾîš mēʿal kissēʾ yiśrāʾēl* 'there shall not be cut off from you ... a man on the throne of Yisra'el': the promise of 2 Sam 7:12-16 in conditional form. The second *lēʾmōr* ('he said') resumes the quotation after the condition.

paragraphs.text: וְגַ֣ם אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁר־עָ֨שָׂה לִ֜י יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה לִשְׁנֵֽי־שָׂרֵ֣י צִבְא֣וֹת יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל לְאַבְנֵ֨ר בֶּן־נֵ֜ר וְלַעֲמָשָׂ֤א בֶן־יֶ֙תֶר֙ וַיַּ֣הַרְגֵ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דְּמֵֽי־מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֞ן דְּמֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֗ה בַּחֲגֹֽרָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמָתְנָ֔יו וּֽבְנַעֲל֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Moreover you know also what Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah did to me, what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Yisra'el, to Avner the son of Ner and to Amasa the son of Yeter, whom he killed, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war on his girdle that was about his waist and on his sandals that were on his feet.

notes.official: Names: Avner = Abner; Ner; Amasa; Yeter = Jether. *śārê ṣiḇʾôṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'the captains of the hosts of Yisra'el', plural *ṣəḇāʾôṯ* (cf. 1:19). *wayyāśem dəmê-milḥāmâ bəšālōm* 'and shed the blood of war in peace', literally 'set': Yo'av killed both men in peacetime as if in battle (2 Sam 3:27; 20:10). The blood on 'his girdle' and 'his sandals' marks the guilt as Yo'av's; the LXX reads 'my girdle ... my sandals', which makes David the bearer of the bloodguilt.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ כְּחָכְמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־תוֹרֵ֧ד שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּשָׁלֹ֖ם שְׁאֹֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Do therefore according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to She'ol in peace.

notes.official: *wəlōʾ-ṯôrēḏ śêḇāṯô bəšālōm šəʾōl* 'and do not let his gray head go down to She'ol in peace' (central `sheol-underworld-realm-of-the-dead`). 'According to your wisdom' (*ḥoḵmâ*) anticipates the wisdom theme of ch. 3. The Masoretic section mark (ס) follows.

paragraphs.text: וְלִבְנֵ֨י בַרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־חֶ֔סֶד וְהָי֖וּ בְּאֹכְלֵ֣י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ כִּי־כֵן֙ קָרְב֣וּ אֵלַ֔י בְּבָרְחִ֕י מִפְּנֵ֖י אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gil'adite, and let them be among those who eat at your table; for so they came near to me when I fled from Avshalom your brother.

notes.official: *taʿăśeh-ḥeseḏ* 'show kindness' (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`): loyalty repaid for Barzillai's provisioning of David at Machanayim (2 Sam 17:27-29; 19:31-39). 'Barzillai the Gil'adite' (ASV 'the Gileadite'); gentilics take '-ite' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *bəʾōḵlê šulḥāneḵā* 'among those who eat at your table', a court pension (2 Sam 9:7).

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה עִ֠מְּךָ שִֽׁמְעִ֨י בֶן־גֵּרָ֥א בֶן־הַיְמִינִי֮ מִבַּחֻרִים֒ וְה֤וּא קִֽלְלַ֙נִי֙ קְלָלָ֣ה נִמְרֶ֔צֶת בְּי֖וֹם לֶכְתִּ֣י מַחֲנָ֑יִם וְהֽוּא־יָרַ֤ד לִקְרָאתִי֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וָאֶשָּׁ֨בַֽע ל֤וֹ בַֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִם־אֲמִֽיתְךָ֖ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

i18n.en: And behold, there is with you Shim'i the son of Gera, the Binyaminite, of Bachurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I went to Machanayim; but he came down to meet me at the Yarden, and I swore to him by YHWH, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'

notes.official: Names: Gera; 'the Binyaminite' (ASV 'the Benjamite'); Bachurim = Bahurim; Machanayim = Mahanaim; Yarden = Jordan. *qəlālâ nimreṣeṯ* 'a grievous curse' (2 Sam 16:5-13; 19:16-23). David's oath not to kill Shim'i 'with the sword' (2 Sam 19:23) is honoured to the letter while the matter passes to Shelomoh.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־תְּנַקֵּ֔הוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם אָ֑תָּה וְיָֽדַעְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לּ֔וֹ וְהוֹרַדְתָּ֧ אֶת־שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּדָ֖ם שְׁאֽוֹל׃

i18n.en: Now therefore do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man; and you will know what you ought to do to him, and you shall bring his gray head down to She'ol with blood."

notes.official: *ʾal-tənaqqēhû* 'do not hold him guiltless' (Piel of *nqh*, 'leave unpunished'). *bəḏām šəʾôl* 'down to She'ol with blood', i.e. by a violent death (central `sheol-underworld-realm-of-the-dead`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב דָּוִ֖ד עִם־אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.

notes.official: 'And David slept with his fathers' (central `shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula`). 'The city of David' is the fortified hill taken in 2 Sam 5:7, 9. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows the death notice.

paragraphs.text: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ דָּוִד֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם מָלַ֔ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֹ֖שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the days that David reigned over Yisra'el were forty years: in Hevron he reigned seven years, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years.

notes.official: Hevron = Hebron (genesis-woh spelling); Yerushalayim = Jerusalem. 'Seven years' rounds the seven years and six months of 2 Sam 5:5.

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֕ה יָשַׁ֕ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֖א דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַתִּכֹּ֥ן מַלְכֻת֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And Shelomoh sat on the throne of David his father; and his kingdom was firmly established.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־חַגֵּ֗ית אֶל־בַּת־שֶׁ֙בַע֙ אֵם־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הֲשָׁל֣וֹם בֹּאֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: Then Adoniyahu the son of Chaggit came to Bat-Sheva the mother of Shelomoh. And she said, "Do you come in peace?" And he said, "In peace."

notes.official: *hăšālôm bōʾeḵā* 'Do you come in peace?', the wary greeting of 1 Sam 16:4. The central `pilegesh-concubine-status-class` entry cites vv 13-25; the Hebrew never calls Avishag a *pîlegeš*, and the line follows the text ('as wife', v 17).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דָּבָ֥ר לִ֖י אֵלָ֑יִךְ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: And he said, "I have something to say to you." And she said, "Speak."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַ֤תְּ יָדַ֙עַתְּ֙ כִּי־לִי֙ הָיְתָ֣ה הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה וְעָלַ֞י שָׂ֧מוּ כָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם לִמְלֹ֑ךְ וַתִּסֹּ֤ב הַמְּלוּכָה֙ וַתְּהִ֣י לְאָחִ֔י כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה הָ֥יְתָה לּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Yisra'el set their faces on me, that I should reign; but the kingdom has turned about and become my brother's, for it was his from YHWH.

notes.official: *kî-lî hāyəṯâ hamməlûḵâ* 'that the kingdom was mine': Adoniyahu claims the succession by seniority (1:6) and concedes it was Shelomoh's 'from YHWH'.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁאֵלָ֤ה אַחַת֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֵ֣ל מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל־תָּשִׁ֖בִי אֶת־פָּנָ֑י וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דַּבֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: And now I ask one request of you; do not deny me." And she said to him, "Speak."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִמְרִי־נָא֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְיִתֶּן־לִ֛י אֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֥ג הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֖ית לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Speak, I pray you, to Shelomoh the king, for he will not deny you, that he give me Avishag the Shunammite as wife."

notes.official: *ləʾiššâ* 'as wife'. To take a king's woman was to claim his throne (2 Sam 3:7; 12:8; 16:21-22), and Shelomoh reads the request that way (v 22).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר בַּת־שֶׁ֖בַע ט֑וֹב אָנֹכִ֕י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And Bat-Sheva said, "Good; I will speak for you to the king."

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֤א בַת־שֶׁ֙בַע֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לְדַבֶּר־ל֖וֹ עַל־אֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיָּקָם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ לִקְרָאתָ֜הּ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֣חוּ לָ֗הּ וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם כִּסֵּא֙ לְאֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב לִֽימִינֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: So Bat-Sheva went to King Shelomoh to speak to him for Adoniyahu. And the king rose up to meet her and bowed himself to her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a throne to be set for the king's mother; and she sat at his right hand.

notes.official: *wayyāśem kissēʾ ləʾēm hammeleḵ* 'and caused a throne to be set for the king's mother': the queen mother (*gəḇîrâ*, 15:13) had a recognized seat at the king's right hand.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שְׁאֵלָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֶ֣לֶת מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל־תָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּֽאמֶר־לָ֤הּ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ שַׁאֲלִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֥י לֹֽא־אָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־פָּנָֽיִךְ׃

i18n.en: Then she said, "I ask one small request of you; do not deny me." And the king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not deny you."

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר יֻתַּ֖ן אֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֣ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֑ית לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֥הוּ אָחִ֖יךָ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And she said, "Let Avishag the Shunammite be given to Adoniyahu your brother as wife."

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעַן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִמּ֗וֹ וְלָמָה֩ אַ֨תְּ שֹׁאֶ֜לֶת אֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֤ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּית֙ לַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ וְשַֽׁאֲלִי־לוֹ֙ אֶת־הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָחִ֖י הַגָּד֣וֹל מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְלוֹ֙ וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וּלְיוֹאָ֖ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And King Shelomoh answered and said to his mother, "And why do you ask Avishag the Shunammite for Adoniyahu? Ask for him the kingdom also, for he is my elder brother; even for him, and for Evyatar the priest, and for Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah."

notes.official: *wəšaʾălî-lô ʾeṯ-hamməlûḵâ* 'Ask for him the kingdom also'. *wəlô ûləʾeḇyāṯār hakkōhēn ûləyôʾāḇ* 'even for him, and for Evyatar the priest, and for Yo'av': an elliptical clause that some versions expand; the MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַע֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י בְנַפְשׁ֔וֹ דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: Then King Shelomoh swore by YHWH, saying, "So may Elohim do to me, and more also, if Adoniyahu has not spoken this word against his own life.

notes.official: *kōh yaʿăśeh-llî ʾĕlōhîm wəḵōh yôsîp̄* 'So may Elohim do to me, and more also': the self-imprecation formula, sworn here 'by YHWH' and with a singular verb, so the referent is YHWH and the anarthrous noun is 'Elohim' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 2). Contrast Izevel's oath at 19:2, where the same formula has plural verbs and is rendered 'So may the elohim do'. *kî ḇənap̄šô* 'against his own life', i.e. at the cost of his life (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה חַי־יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֱכִינַ֗נִי ויושיביני [וַיּֽוֹשִׁיבַ֙נִי֙] עַל־כִּסֵּא֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וַאֲשֶׁ֧ר עָֽשָׂה־לִ֛י בַּ֖יִת כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר כִּ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם יוּמַ֖ת אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: Now therefore, as YHWH lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house, as he promised, surely Adoniyahu shall be put to death this day."

notes.official: Ketiv *wywšybyny* (plene, with an extra yod), Qere *wayyôšîḇanî* 'and set me': orthographic; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *ḥay-YHWH* 'as YHWH lives' (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`, which cites this verse). *wəʾăšer ʿāśâ-lî bayiṯ* 'and who has made me a house': the dynasty promised in 2 Sam 7:11-16.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד בְּנָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וַיִּפְגַּע־בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And King Shelomoh sent by the hand of Benayahu the son of Yehoyada; and he fell upon him, and he died.

notes.official: *wayyip̄gaʿ-bô* 'and he fell upon him', the verb of attack (also vv 29, 31, 34, 46). The Masoretic section mark (ס) follows.

paragraphs.text: וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲנָתֹת֙ לֵ֣ךְ עַל־שָׂדֶ֔יךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ מָ֖וֶת אָ֑תָּה וּבַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה לֹ֣א אֲמִיתֶ֗ךָ כִּֽי־נָשָׂ֜אתָ אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ לִפְנֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וְכִ֣י הִתְעַנִּ֔יתָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְעַנָּ֖ה אָבִֽי׃

i18n.en: And to Evyatar the priest the king said, "Go to Anatot, to your own fields; for you are a man worthy of death; but I will not at this time put you to death, because you carried the ark of the Lord YHWH before David my father, and because you were afflicted in all in which my father was afflicted."

notes.official: *ʾărôn ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'the ark of the Lord YHWH': after *ʾăḏōnāy* the MT points the name with the vowels of *ʾĕlōhîm* (*yĕhōwih*), the standing reading for the doubled divine name (central `adonai-yhwh-divine-name`). *ʾîš māweṯ ʾāttâ* 'you are a man worthy of death', literally 'a man of death'. Anatot = Anathoth, the priestly town of Binyamin (Jer 1:1). Evyatar had shared David's flight (1 Sam 22:20-23; 2 Sam 15:24-29).

paragraphs.text: וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת־אֶבְיָתָ֔ר מִהְי֥וֹת כֹּהֵ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְמַלֵּא֙ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֛ר עַל־בֵּ֥ית עֵלִ֖י בְּשִׁלֹֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So Shelomoh drove out Evyatar from being priest to YHWH, to fulfill the word of YHWH which he had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

notes.official: *ləmallēʾ ʾeṯ-dəḇar YHWH* 'to fulfil the word of YHWH ... concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh': the oracle of 1 Sam 2:27-36, one of the prophecy-and-fulfilment links that structure Kings (von Rad, *Studies in Deuteronomy*, 1953). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows.

paragraphs.text: וְהַשְּׁמֻעָה֙ בָּ֣אָה עַד־יוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֣י יוֹאָ֗ב נָטָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲדֹנִיָּ֔ה וְאַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לֹ֣א נָטָ֑ה וַיָּ֤נָס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And the report came to Yo'av, for Yo'av had turned after Adoniyahu, though after Avshalom he had not turned. And Yo'av fled to the Tent of YHWH and caught hold of the horns of the altar.

notes.official:
MT *kî yôʾāḇ nāṭâ ʾaḥărê ʾăḏōniyyâ wəʾaḥărê ʾaḇšālôm lōʾ nāṭâ* 'for Yo'av had turned after Adoniyahu, though after Avshalom he had not turned' (ASV likewise). Greek witnesses, the Syriac and the Vulgate read 'after Shelomoh he had not turned', which states the disloyalty more directly. The MT is construable and is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). MT short name form, normalized (1:5).

*wayyānos yôʾāḇ ʾel-ʾōhel YHWH wayyaḥăzēq bəqarnôṯ hammizbēaḥ* 'And Yo'av fled to the Tent of YHWH and caught hold of the horns of the altar' (`qarnot-ha-mizbeach-horns-of-the-altar-cross-corpus`). The asylum law of Ex 21:14 excludes a deliberate killer ('you shall take him from my altar, that he may die'), which is the ground on which Shelomoh acts (vv 29-34).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) cites this verse with 1:50 as a description of handling the levers of a transmitter-receiver to make contact with the creators. The line keeps the literal 'horns of the altar', as at 1:50, and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיֻּגַּ֞ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כִּ֣י נָ֤ס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע לֵאמֹ֖ר לֵ֥ךְ פְּגַע־בּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it was told King Shelomoh that Yo'av had fled to the Tent of YHWH, and behold, he is beside the altar. Then Shelomoh sent Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, saying, "Go, fall upon him."

notes.official: *wəhinnēh ʾēṣel hammizbēaḥ* 'and behold, he is beside the altar'. The LXX adds an exchange in which Shelomoh asks Yo'av why he fled to the altar and Yo'av answers that he feared the king; it is not in the MT and is not translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א בְנָיָ֜הוּ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ צֵ֔א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ׀ לֹ֖א כִּ֣י פֹ֣ה אָמ֑וּת וַיָּ֨שֶׁב בְּנָיָ֤הוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ דָּבָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה־דִבֶּ֥ר יוֹאָ֖ב וְכֹ֥ה עָנָֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And Benayahu came to the Tent of YHWH and said to him, "Thus says the king, 'Come out.'" And he said, "No; for here I will die." And Benayahu brought the king word again, saying, "Thus said Yo'av, and thus he answered me."

notes.official: *kōh-ʾāmar hammeleḵ ṣēʾ* 'Thus says the king, Come out', the royal messenger formula. *kî p̄ōh ʾāmûṯ* 'for here I will die': Yo'av refuses to leave the sanctuary.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲשֵׂה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר וּפְגַע־בּ֖וֹ וּקְבַרְתּ֑וֹ וַהֲסִירֹ֣תָ ׀ דְּמֵ֣י חִנָּ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁפַ֣ךְ יוֹאָ֔ב מֵעָלַ֕י וּמֵעַ֖ל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

i18n.en: And the king said to him, "Do as he has said, and fall upon him, and bury him; that you may take away from me and from my father's house the blood which Yo'av shed without cause.

notes.official: *dəmê ḥinnām* 'the blood ... shed without cause' (literally 'blood of gratuitousness'): bloodguilt that would rest on David's house unless avenged (Num 35:33; Deut 19:13).

paragraphs.text: וְהֵשִׁיב֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־דָּמ֜וֹ עַל־רֹאשׁ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגַ֣ע בִּשְׁנֵֽי־אֲ֠נָשִׁים צַדִּקִ֨ים וְטֹבִ֤ים מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ וַיַּהַרְגֵ֣ם בַּחֶ֔רֶב וְאָבִ֥י דָוִ֖ד לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע אֶת־אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־נֵר֙ שַׂר־צְבָ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־עֲמָשָׂ֥א בֶן־יֶ֖תֶר שַׂר־צְבָ֥א יְהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH will return his blood upon his own head, because he fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword, and my father David did not know it: Avner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Yisra'el, and Amasa the son of Yeter, captain of the host of Yehudah.

notes.official: Avner, 'captain of the host of Yisra'el', and Amasa, 'captain of the host of Yehudah' (*śar-ṣəḇāʾ*, cf. 1:19).

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁ֤בוּ דְמֵיהֶם֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹאָ֔ב וּבְרֹ֥אשׁ זַרְע֖וֹ לְעֹלָ֑ם וּלְדָוִ֡ד וּ֠לְזַרְעוֹ וּלְבֵית֨וֹ וּלְכִסְא֜וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁל֛וֹם עַד־עוֹלָ֖ם מֵעִ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: So shall their blood return upon the head of Yo'av and upon the head of his seed forever; but to David, and to his seed, and to his house, and to his throne, there shall be peace forever from YHWH."

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֗עַל בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיִּפְגַּע־בּ֖וֹ וַיְמִתֵ֑הוּ וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּבֵית֖וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

i18n.en: Then Benayahu the son of Yehoyada went up and fell upon him and put him to death; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

notes.official: *wayyiqqāḇēr bəḇêṯô bammiḏbār* 'and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness', i.e. on his estate in the steppe of Yehudah.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע תַּחְתָּ֖יו עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וְאֶת־צָד֤וֹק הַכֹּהֵן֙ נָתַ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תַּ֖חַת אֶבְיָתָֽר׃

i18n.en: And the king put Benayahu the son of Yehoyada in his place over the host; and Tzadoq the priest the king put in the place of Evyatar.

notes.official: *ʿal-haṣṣāḇāʾ* 'over the host' (1:19). Tzadoq replaces Evyatar, completing the fulfilment of v 27. The LXX inserts here the first of its long supplements (3 Kgdms 2:35a-o); see v 46.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֔י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ בְּֽנֵה־לְךָ֥ בַ֙יִת֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֖ שָׁ֑ם וְלֹֽא־תֵצֵ֥א מִשָּׁ֖ם אָ֥נֶה וָאָֽנָה׃

i18n.en: And the king sent and called for Shim'i, and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Yerushalayim, and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְעָֽבַרְתָּ֙ אֶת־נַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת דָּמְךָ֖ יִהְיֶ֥ה בְרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

i18n.en: For on the day you go out and cross the brook Qidron, know for certain that you shall surely die; your blood shall be upon your own head."

notes.official: *naḥal qiḏrôn* 'the brook Qidron' = Kidron, the valley east of the city on the road to Bachurim and Binyamin. *môṯ tāmûṯ* 'you shall surely die' (central `mot-tamut`). *dāməḵā yihyeh ḇərōʾšeḵā* 'your blood shall be upon your own head': no bloodguilt will fall on the executioner.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְעִ֤י לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ ט֣וֹב הַדָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב שִׁמְעִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Shim'i said to the king, "The word is good; as my lord the king has said, so will your servant do." And Shim'i dwelt in Yerushalayim many days.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וַיִּבְרְח֤וּ שְׁנֵֽי־עֲבָדִים֙ לְשִׁמְעִ֔י אֶל־אָכִ֥ישׁ בֶּֽן־מַעֲכָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ גַּ֑ת וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לְשִׁמְעִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בְּגַֽת׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass at the end of three years that two of Shim'i's servants ran away to Akhish the son of Ma'akhah, king of Gat. And they told Shim'i, saying, "Behold, your servants are in Gat."

notes.official: Akhish = Achish; Ma'akhah = Maacah; Gat = Gath, the Philistine city whose king of the same name sheltered David (1 Sam 27:2, there 'son of Ma'okh').

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣קָם שִׁמְעִ֗י וַֽיַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ אֶת־חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ גַּ֙תָה֙ אֶל־אָכִ֔ישׁ לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְעִ֔י וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־עֲבָדָ֖יו מִגַּֽת׃

i18n.en: And Shim'i arose and saddled his donkey, and went to Gat to Akhish to seek his servants; and Shim'i went and brought his servants from Gat.

notes.official: *wayyaḥăḇōš ʾeṯ-ḥămōrô* 'and saddled his donkey' (ASV 'ass'; 'donkey' also at 13:13-29).

paragraphs.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה כִּי־הָלַ֨ךְ שִׁמְעִ֧י מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם גַּ֖ת וַיָּשֹֽׁב׃

i18n.en: And it was told Shelomoh that Shim'i had gone from Yerushalayim to Gat and had come back.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֗י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲל֧וֹא הִשְׁבַּעְתִּ֣יךָ בַֽיהוָ֗ה וָאָעִ֤ד בְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אָ֣נֶה וָאָ֔נָה יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וַתֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלַ֛י ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

i18n.en: And the king sent and called for Shim'i, and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by YHWH, and warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and walk anywhere, know for certain that you shall surely die'? And you said to me, 'The word that I have heard is good.'

notes.official: *hălôʾ hišbaʿtîḵā ḇYHWH wāʾāʿiḏ bəḵā* 'Did I not make you swear by YHWH, and warn you': *hēʿîḏ bə-* 'solemnly warn' (ASV 'protested unto thee'). The central `haed-heid-solemn-warning-formula` cites this verse; its Gen 43:3 wording ('did solemnly protest') is not imported. *môṯ tāmûṯ* as v 37 (central `mot-tamut`).

paragraphs.text: וּמַדּ֕וּעַ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֵ֖ת שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־הַמִּצְוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּ֥יתִי עָלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Why then have you not kept the oath of YHWH and the commandment with which I charged you?"

notes.official: *šəḇuʿaṯ YHWH* 'the oath of YHWH', the oath sworn by YHWH (v 42).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־שִׁמְעִ֗י אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָדַע֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ לְדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וְהֵשִׁ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־רָעָתְךָ֖ בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

i18n.en: And the king said to Shim'i, "You know all the evil which your heart knows, which you did to David my father; therefore YHWH shall return your evil upon your own head.

notes.official: *ʾēṯ kol-hārāʿâ ʾăšer yāḏaʿ ləḇāḇəḵā* 'all the evil which your heart knows'. *wəhēšîḇ YHWH ʾeṯ-rāʿāṯəḵā bərōʾšeḵā* 'therefore YHWH shall return your evil upon your own head' (cf. v 32).

paragraphs.text: וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בָּר֑וּךְ וְכִסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֛וֹן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: But King Shelomoh shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before YHWH forever."

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶת־בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַיִּפְגַּע־בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה נָכ֖וֹנָה בְּיַד־שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

i18n.en: So the king commanded Benayahu the son of Yehoyada; and he went out and fell upon him, and he died. And the kingdom was established in the hand of Shelomoh.

notes.official: *wəhammamlāḵâ nāḵônâ bəyaḏ-šəlōmōh* 'And the kingdom was established in the hand of Shelomoh': with v 12 it closes the succession narrative. The LXX has a second long supplement here (3 Kgdms 2:46a-l), a summary of Shelomoh's wisdom, provisions and officials that largely parallels MT 1 Kgs 4-5 and 9. The translation follows the MT and does not render the Greek supplements (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).
